questions.q: What is Azure SQL Database, per this lesson?
options: A single, fully-managed database (or elastic pool of them) — the most PaaS option with the least SQL Server surface area
A full virtual machine with SQL Server installed on it
An instance-level PaaS product with near-100% SQL Server surface
A purely on-prem product unrelated to Azure
questions.explain: Azure SQL Database is database-scoped, not instance-scoped — no SQL Server Agent or cross-database queries by default.

questions.q: What does Azure SQL Managed Instance give you that Azure SQL Database does not?
options: Near-100% of SQL Server's instance-level surface — cross-database queries, SQL Server Agent, CLR, linked servers — while remaining PaaS
Full control over the underlying operating system
Nothing different — it is functionally identical to Azure SQL Database
A guarantee of zero deployment time
questions.explain: Managed Instance exists because Azure SQL Database's database-scoped model is too narrow for some real migrations that depend on instance-level features.

questions.q: What does SQL Server on an Azure VM require you to manage that the other two options do not?
options: The operating system and the SQL Server instance yourself — patching, backups (unless automated), and HA/DR configuration, same as on-prem
Nothing — it is fully managed by Microsoft like the other two options
Only the database schema, same level of management as Azure SQL Database
The physical hardware and hypervisor
questions.explain: SQL Server on a VM is full IaaS: Microsoft owns hardware and the hypervisor, but you're back to owning the OS and SQL Server instance yourself.

questions.q: What extra requirement does Azure SQL Managed Instance have that Azure SQL Database and SQL Server on a VM don't demand in the same way?
options: A dedicated subnet inside a Virtual Network (VNet)
A public IP address with no firewall rules
A separate SQL Server license purchased outside Azure
Manual OS patching performed by the customer
questions.explain: This VNet subnet requirement, along with longer deployment time, is one of Managed Instance's real tradeoffs — covered fully in Lesson 12.

questions.q: According to this lesson's quick decision guide, which option fits a workload that needs SQL Server Agent jobs and cross-database queries but should still be patched and backed up automatically?
options: Azure SQL Managed Instance
Azure SQL Database
SQL Server on an Azure VM
None of the three options support automatic patching
questions.explain: Managed Instance is the option that provides near-full instance-level surface while Microsoft still handles patching and backups.
